column16: The core memory mechanic worked flawlessly. The transition from telling PulsePet a fact ("I like basketball") to having it successfully recalled later was seamless. Additionally, the user interface is incredibly clean and intuitive. Having distinct, highly visible buttons for "Clear Chat" and "Clear Memory" is a fantastic design choice that gives the user immediate confidence and control over their data.
column17: I would love to see the memory feature integrated more organically into casual conversation. Right now, it works great as a direct query ("What do I like?"), but it would be amazing if the AI proactively used that information. For example, if I ask for a joke after telling it I like basketball, it would be cool if it spontaneously generated a basketball-themed joke without me having to ask for one specifically. Also, integrating the chat interface directly alongside the animated Unity avatar would really bring the companion aspect to life.
column18: Honestly, nothing was difficult to use—the minimalist UI is perfect for a prototype and keeps the focus on the functionality. If I had to nitpick, it might be helpful to have a small visual indicator (like a little save icon or a subtle flash) that pops up when PulsePet actively commits something to its long-term memory, just to distinguish it from a standard conversational response.
column19: Yes, definitely. Most standard chatbots feel like you are interacting with a blank slate every time you talk to them. Because PulsePet can hold onto a specific user preference and bring it up later, it bridges the gap between a generic search tool and an actual "companion." It creates a sense of continuity and makes the user feel listened to.
column20: Great job on the prototype, and good luck with the rest of your dissertation write-up! The foundation you've built is incredibly solid. The combination of persistent memory with strict, user-facing data controls (like the clear memory button) is highly relevant to current discussions in AI ethics and HCI. You've demonstrated the concept perfectly!
